text:
anya: deploy-bot just flagged an odd p95 jump in the EU canary after the rollout. Auto-rollback queued. We have a large reserved customer on the same AV. Hold auto-action; need quick plan. :thinking:

deploy-bot: ALERT: latency.p95_eu_canary = 395ms (+39%). Auto-rollback scheduled in 4m unless acknowledged. slice=eu-canary

rafa: Holding auto-rollback. Do not revert global. Proposal: split traffic, pin reserved-customer hosts to current build, perform segmented rollback on non-reserved canary hosts only.

ops-runner: Will run segmented rollback. Steps: 1) list non-reserved canary hosts 2) snapshot 3) promote those hosts to v2.9.0-rollback 4) monitor 15m window. Command: `deployctl promote --hosts @non_reserved --version v2.9.0-rollback --serial`

product-ops: Note for release notes: "Partial rollback applied to non-reserved EU canary nodes to mitigate p95 regression; reserved-customer nodes pinned."

cs-liaison: Notifying customer with a short, non-technical line now.

ops-runner: Segmented rollback started. 2/6 hosts reverted. Monitoring telemetry.

deploy-bot: job=prom-4945-123 progress=33% targets=6

ops-runner: All targets rolled back. p95 trending back toward baseline within 8m. No error spike.

anya: Keep reserved nodes pinned for 24h and resume rollout only after two stable windows. Capture this flow in runbook: "segmented rollback when reserved customers present." Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
